claims.statement: NIS2 covers medium and large entities across many critical sectors and requires cybersecurity risk-management measures and significant-incident notification, expanding the compliance surface beyond traditional digital infrastructure.

NIS2 explicitly includes supply-chain security and supplier relationships among the core risk-management elements, supporting a focused supplier-evidence wedge rather than another broad security dashboard.

Hypothesis: MSPs can distribute and maintain a supplier passport more efficiently than a standalone vendor because they already administer controls and evidence for multiple clients and benefit from standardised reviews.

contrary_evidence: Member-state transposition remains uneven, so the exact buyer obligation and enforcement timing differ by jurisdiction.
Governance, risk, and compliance suites already provide questionnaire automation; the passport must win through MSP distribution and reusable evidence rather than feature breadth.

economics.acquisition_route: Recruit a small number of sector-focused MSPs or brokers, each activating dozens of clients and hundreds of suppliers
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 10000 active supplier passports at 55 PLN monthly net revenue equals 6.6 million PLN ARR in years 6-8; at 25% EBITDA, 6x EBITDA, and 70% ownership, founder equity would be about 6.9 million PLN
economics.founder_time: 18-24 hours weekly for secure MVP and mappings, then 8-12 hours weekly with MSP-owned remediation and onboarding
economics.gross_margin_basis: Evidence storage, mapping, and reminders can support 80-90% gross margin if partners handle remediation consulting
economics.payback: Target under 9 months per channel partner; their payback comes from replacing repeated questionnaire labour and adding a managed-service line
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 40-120 PLN per supplier monthly with 30000-100000 PLN annual MSP minimums
economics.retention_or_repeat: Assertions expire, controls change, and annual supplier reviews recur; the evidence history raises switching cost

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Control-to-question mappings, expiring evidence lineage, and reciprocal passport acceptance reduce marginal review effort across the network
fingerprint.customer: European MSPs, cyber-insurance brokers, NIS2-scope organisations, and their material suppliers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: White-labelled inside MSP managed-security packages and cyber-insurance risk-improvement programmes
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Reusable permissioned security-evidence graph and questionnaire-mapping SaaS sold through MSPs
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: MSP or insured organisation pays per managed supplier passport and annual evidence renewal
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A supplier onboarding or annual review needs current evidence for supply-chain cybersecurity controls

founder_fit: Good fit for structured evidence, automation, and low-camera B2B work, with channel partners doing much of the relationship management. Security architecture and independent review require specialist help; the founder should not represent the tool as certification.
risks: A breach following a positive passport assertion could create severe trust and liability damage.
Sensitive security documents make the product an attractive attack target.
Large MSP platforms could internalise the workflow after channel validation.

structure.commercial_archetype: Reusable B2B credential and evidence network
structure.control_point: The supplier-security approval and renewal record inside an MSP-managed client workflow
structure.critical_dependency: Partner and customer trust in secure permissioning, assertion provenance, and non-certification liability boundaries

thesis: Offer MSPs and cyber-insurance brokers a reusable evidence graph for NIS2 supplier security. A managed client answers and evidences core controls once; the partner maps that passport into customer questionnaires, annual reviews, policy gaps, and incident-ready contact chains, with every assertion carrying an owner, expiry date, and source document.
title: Supplier Security Passport
uncertainties: Which supply-chain questionnaires converge enough to support automated mappings is untested.
MSP revenue share and appetite to white-label a third-party evidence layer are unknown.
Customers may resist sharing evidence across counterparties even with granular permissioning.
